definitions.explanation: A professional chef, particularly one trained in Japanese cuisine (washoku). Refers to a skilled cook who works at a counter or in a kitchen of a Japanese restaurant. The term carries connotations of craftsmanship and traditional skill.

examples.english: The chef at that restaurant is very skilled.

examples.japanese: ⟦{父|ちち}→父：00566_chichi⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{寿司屋|すしや}→寿司屋：10166_sushiya⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{板前|いたまえ}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: My father works as a sushi chef.

examples.japanese: ⟦{一流|いちりゅう}→一流：03009_ichiryuu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{板前|いたまえ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧、⟦{何年|なんねん}→何年：12737_nannen⟧⟦も→も：00484_mo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{修業|しゅぎょう}→修業：16906_shugyou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{必要|ひつよう}→必要：00846_hitsuyou⟧だ。
examples.english: It takes many years of training to become a top-class chef.

notes:
ETYMOLOGY:
⟦{板|いた}→板：01792_ita⟧ (board, cutting board) + ⟦{前|まえ}→前：02255_mae⟧ (in front of). Originally referred to the person standing in front of the cutting board — the cook.

USAGE:
{板前|いたまえ} specifically refers to chefs of Japanese cuisine and carries a sense of traditional craftsmanship. For Western-style chefs, ⟦シェフ→シェフ：05062_shefu⟧ or ⟦コック→コック：05063_kokku⟧ is more common. ⟦{料理人|りょうりにん}→料理人：19396_ryourinin⟧ is a more general term for any professional cook.

CULTURAL NOTE:
In traditional Japanese restaurants, the {板前|いたまえ} often works at a counter (⟦カウンター→カウンター：10816_kauntaa⟧) in view of customers, especially at sushi restaurants. The term implies years of apprenticeship and mastery of knife skills.
